doc.title: Marian McPartland interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, April 26, 1997

title: Choosing album concepts: Strayhorn and Benny Carter
summary: Her Strayhorn record and the Benny Carter record Carl Jefferson of Concord opposed.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you usually have a concept beforehand when the opportunity to record comes up, and you’re thinking about your next album, do you think in a broad sense, this album is going to be about standards or it’s going to be — you know — how do you decide that sort of thing?

Oh, let’s see. Well a few years back I had this, I did have an idea, I wanted to do tunes by Billy Strayhorn because it seemed like nobody had. And it turned out that I and Art Farmer were sort of the sole people who had done an entire record of Billy Strayhorn’s music. And I feel rather proud of myself for that. And of course now it’s happening all over the place and they’re going to make a movie about him, so I’m really glad all of this is happening. And then I don’t know really why, I guess I had met Benny Carter finally and for some reason or other I really wanted to do a record of Benny Carter’s music. And Carl Jefferson at Concord, he was dead against it. One of his reasons were, “oh Benny wants so much money,” and well he just was against it. But I really wanted to do it, so I finally did do it. And Benny has nice tunes, really good tunes.
